Species level refers to organisms sharing a species, not their internal organization.
Organs and organ systems work together within an individual organism.
A population consists of members of one species in an area.
A community consists of populations of different species.
Protein is a macromolecule made of amino acids.
Starch is a macromolecule made of glucose units.
Glucose is a small molecule and is therefore a micromolecule.
Lipids are generally large biological molecules, not the intended micromolecule here.
Observation is an earlier step used to formulate a hypothesis.
Deduction follows a hypothesis and leads to testable predictions.
A theory is not the immediate next step after a hypothesis in the biological method.
A law is not the immediate next step after a hypothesis.
G1 is primarily a growth phase before DNA replication.
G2 follows DNA replication and prepares the cell for division.
DNA is replicated and chromosomes are duplicated during S phase.
G0 is a resting or non-dividing state.
An X-ray is an imaging method using X-rays, not a microscope photograph.
Ultrasound creates images using sound waves, not a microscope.
A photograph taken through a microscope is called a micrograph.
A radiograph is an image produced using radiation such as X-rays.
Asterias rubens is a sea star, not onion.
Allium cepa is the scientific name of onion.
Corvus splendens is the house crow.
Homo sapiens is the human species.
The parasite reaches the salivary glands for transmission, but its major multiplication in the mosquito occurs earlier.
The intestine is not the usual named site for the parasite's multiplication in the mosquito.
Plasmodium develops and multiplies in oocysts on the mosquito's stomach wall.
The mouth is not where Plasmodium multiplies.
Vitamin B deficiency causes other disorders, not scurvy.
Vitamin A deficiency is associated with vision problems, not scurvy.
Vitamin D deficiency can cause rickets or osteomalacia, not scurvy.
Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.
Glycolysis does not take place in the nucleus.
Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins and are not the site of glycolysis.
Centrioles help organize cell division and are not the site of glycolysis.
30°C–35°C is not the high-temperature range typically associated with stomatal closure in this question.
Temperatures of 40°C–45°C can cause stomata to close to reduce water loss.
10°C–15°C is not the expected temperature range for heat-induced stomatal closure.
20°C–25°C is generally moderate and does not typically cause this heat response.
Prions are infectious agents composed only of protein.
Viruses contain genetic material as well as a protein coat.
Bacteria are cells containing many types of molecules, not protein alone.
Viroids are composed of RNA, not protein.
Chromatin is DNA associated with proteins, not spindle fibers.
A kinetochore is a chromosome structure where spindle fibers attach.
Cleavage refers to cell division or cleavage furrow formation, not the spindle apparatus.
The complete set of spindle fibers is called the mitotic spindle.
Pepsin is not active in the intestine as its main site of action.
Pepsin digests proteins in the acidic environment of the stomach.
The oesophagus transports food and is not where pepsin works.
The mouth contains enzymes such as salivary amylase, not pepsin.
Cellulose is a major component of plant cell walls, not typical prokaryotic walls.
Most prokaryotic cell walls are composed of peptidoglycan.
Lignin strengthens some plant cell walls and is not found in prokaryotic walls.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls, not prokaryotic cell walls.
